name: Denmark

legislature.name: Folketing (179)
legislature.detail: Supported by Red–Green Alliance, Alternative and Greenlandic/Faroese members.

synopsis: Frederiksen began a third term in June 2026 at the head of a four-party centre-left minority government. Greenland and rapid military build-up top the agenda after a crisis over US designs on the territory.
policies: Greenland negotiations with the US and Greenland's government

name: Greenland (Denmark)
system: Autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark with parliamentary self-government
judiciary: Greenland courts within the Danish legal system.
synopsis: A broad national-unity coalition governs in response to US interest in acquiring Greenland. The long-term goal of independence is shared but its pace is debated.
policies: Resisting annexation while expanding US/Danish cooperation
challenges: Economic dependence on Danish block grant

name: Sweden

legislature.name: Riksdag (349)
legislature.control: Opposition parties (S, V, C, MP) 176 vs outgoing Tidö parties (M, SD, KD, L) 173
legislature.detail: S 99, M 70, SD 62, V 30, C 25, KD 22, MP 22, L 19. Speaker Andreas Norlén (M). On 15 Oct 2026 the Riksdag rejected Magdalena Andersson as PM of a Social Democrat-only government, 248 against and 99 in favour. This was the first of the four PM votes allowed before a snap election must be called. Government formation is continuing.

judiciary: Independent courts headed by the Supreme Court and the Supreme Administrative Court; the Council on Legislation reviews draft bills.

elections.name: General election (Riksdag)
elections.note: Turnout 84.9%. Opposition parties won 176 seats against 173 for the Tidö parties. Seats and vote share: S 99 (28.0%), M 70 (19.9%), SD 62 (17.5%), V 30 (8.4%), C 25 (7.0%), KD 22 (6.2%), MP 22 (6.1%), L 19 (5.3%). Kristersson asked to be relieved of office on 17 Sep and now leads a caretaker government.

elections.name: General election (Riksdag)
elections.note: Regular election, held on the second Sunday of September. A snap election would be called if four PM votes fail.

synopsis: The opposition parties (Social Democrats, Left, Centre and Greens) narrowly won the September 2026 election with 176 of 349 seats. They disagree over which parties should sit in government, and on 15 October 2026 the Riksdag rejected Magdalena Andersson as prime minister of a Social Democrat-only government. Ulf Kristersson leads a caretaker government while the Speaker continues talks.
policies: Caretaker government limited to routine business pending a new government
Measures against gang crime (outgoing government's agenda)
NATO integration and higher defence spending
challenges: Government formation deadlock: one failed PM vote so far, and a snap election follows if four fail
Disputes among the opposition parties over whether the Centre or Left Party should be in government
reviewNote: Confirmed: election results, seat counts, Kristersson's caretaker status (still shown as of about 23 Oct 2026) and the 15 Oct PM vote (248–99 against Andersson). Corrected the earlier claim of 'four failed PM votes'; only one vote has been held. Not yet confirmed: who the Speaker gave the next formation mandate to after 15 Oct, and whether any further PM vote is scheduled. Check before the next update.

name: Norway

legislature.name: Storting (169)
legislature.control: Labour minority, relying on centre-left parties
legislature.detail: Progress Party is the largest opposition party.

elections.name: Parliamentary election
elections.note: Labour re-elected; Progress Party surged to second.

synopsis: Støre's Labour Party governs alone in minority, with Jens Stoltenberg as finance minister. The sovereign wealth fund, energy and security dominate.
policies: Ethical guidelines for the sovereign wealth fund

name: Finland
judiciary: Supreme Court and Supreme Administrative Court.
synopsis: Orpo's centre-right coalition is pursuing austerity and labour-market reform, while President Stubb leads foreign and security policy as a NATO frontline state.
policies: NATO integration and border security with Russia

name: Iceland

elections.name: Referendum on resuming EU accession talks (planned)

synopsis: A coalition led by women party leaders is focused on stabilising the economy and plans a referendum on reopening EU accession talks.

name: Estonia
synopsis: Michal's two-party government is very unpopular amid tax rises to fund defence, with Isamaa leading polls ahead of the March 2027 election.

name: Latvia

legislature.name: Saeima (100)
legislature.detail: Oct 2026: United List 41, Latvia First 17, others 10–15 each; coalition talks under way.

elections.name: Saeima election
elections.note: Andris Kulbergs' United List won decisively.

synopsis: The centre-right United List won the October 2026 election by a wide margin, and its leader Andris Kulbergs is expected to form the next government.
reviewNote: New government expected — update prime minister and coalition.

name: Lithuania
synopsis: Ruginienė's Social Democrat-led coalition took over after a business scandal toppled her predecessor; the inclusion of the populist Dawn of Nemunas party has drawn protests.
challenges: Coalition controversy over Dawn of Nemunas
